summary: Cape George light on the Northumberland Strait was first lit in 1861 from a dwelling roof; its octagonal concrete tower dates from 1968, and the Antigonish North Shore Development Association owns it.

lens.note: Third order dioptric triple flashing light by the report for 1908-09 (Sessional Paper No. 21, 1910); an electric lantern from 1992 (NSLPS)

structures.note: Octagonal iron lantern on the roof of a wooden dwelling; ten feet across, eight sides (Sessional Papers of 1875, as parl.ns.ca quotes it). NSLPS calls the first light a square white wooden tower; see notes_for_editor.

Wooden octagonal tower with sloping sides, 54 ft 6 in (16.6 m) to the top of the lantern, and a frame dwelling 26 by 24 ft. Built by contract with E. F. Munro of Westville for $3,097. NSLPS gives the tower as 44 ft.
Octagonal concrete tower, 45 ft (14 m) per NSLPS; the record gives 13.7 m.

access.note: Lighthouse Road, 0.8 km off Route 337 on Cape George Point; grounds open (Lighthouse Friends).

facts.agency: Antigonish North Shore Development Association (NSLPS). Lighthouse Friends' visitor note still names the Canadian Coast Guard; see notes_for_editor.

events.note: First light established; a dwelling topped by an octagonal iron lantern; David Condon appointed first keeper
Superintendent Thomas P. Jose recommended a fixed light; additional supports were added to the lighthouse instead
Second order lens, revolving white (30 s), per NSLPS
Wire-rope stays fitted to the lantern to prevent vibration in storms
Nova Scotia legislature timeline says the first lighthouse was destroyed by fire in 1907. Lighthouse Friends mentions no fire. Disputed; see notes_for_editor.
Department's report for 1906-07 says a third order double flashing light had been received for Cape George and was being erected
New wooden octagonal tower and keeper's dwelling erected; contract price $3,097 (E. F. Munro of Westville)
Catoptric revolving white light discontinued and replaced by a third order dioptric triple flashing light (Department's report for 1908-09)
Contract for a reinforced-concrete tower awarded to Northumberland Construction Ltd., 12 October 1967
New concrete tower placed in operation, 6 June 1968
Light automated; keeper William W. Clark retired
Old 1908 tower and dwelling bulldozed on 7 September 1978; lantern and lens had been removed earlier
Electric lantern with group flashing white (12 s), per NSLPS
Light transferred to the local community (Lighthouse Friends)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1968 date is the present concrete tower. The first light dates from 1861 (Parks Canada statement, Lighthouse Friends, NSLPS).

Lighthouse Friends and the 1875 Sessional Papers (quoted by parl.ns.ca) describe an octagonal iron lantern on a dwelling roof; the NSLPS list calls the first light a square white wooden tower. The story states both.
Lighthouse Friends, parl.ns.ca (quoting the 1909 report) give 54 ft 6 in to the top of the lantern; the NSLPS list gives 44 ft. The story states both.
Lighthouse Friends ties automation and the keeper's retirement to 1968; the NSLPS list says automated by 1993. The story states both.

The 1908 report's entry 'Cape George, third order double flashing light received and being erected' carries no county. The Department's lists also show a Cape George on the Great Bras d'Or Lake, so the entry may be that station. The story says so.

notes_for_editor: No USLHS roster exists for Canada. (1) Do not confuse this light with Cape George on the Bras d'Or Lake (Victoria County), which the Department's reports also list; the 1909 report's 'Cape George, Northumberland Strait' entry is the one used. (2) Keepers: Lighthouse Friends has David Condon 1861-1882, W. Joseph Condon 1882-1889, Hugh McDonald 1889-1898; the provincial page has David Condon 1861-1898 and says the Condon family ran the light for 29 years (the page's own dates do not add up to 29 years for David Condon alone). Falkenham's end date is 1951 in Lighthouse Friends and 1952 in the provincial page; Clark's start date is 1951 in Lighthouse Friends and 1952 in the provincial page. The Department's 1912 table is OCR'd; 'Cape George Alex. McEachern' is read on the same printed line. (3) The 1907 fire: the provincial timeline says the first lighthouse was destroyed by fire in 1907; Lighthouse Friends says nothing about a fire; the Department's report printed in 1908 says a third order double flashing light had been received for Cape George and was being erected, which is consistent with either account. The story reports the claim and the disagreement; no report of the fire was read. (4) The first light's form: NSLPS calls it a square white wooden tower; the NSLPS's own structure entry says 'lantern on roof of wood dwelling'; Lighthouse Friends and the 1875 Sessional Papers (quoted by parl.ns.ca) describe an octagonal iron lantern on the dwelling roof. (5) Second tower height: 54 ft 6 in to the top of the lantern (Lighthouse Friends and the Department's 1909 report), NSLPS 44 ft. (6) Automation: Lighthouse Friends says automated in 1968; NSLPS says automated by 1993. (7) Ownership: NSLPS names the Antigonish North Shore Development Association; Lighthouse Friends' history says the light was transferred to the local community in 2016, while its visitor note still says the Canadian Coast Guard owns it. Parks Canada says the province acquired the surrounding land. (8) Heritage: the record gives a 2015 designation; Lighthouse Friends says the Heritage Lighthouse Protection Act was 'of 2008' but gives no designation date for this light; not used. (9) The Coast Guard list for Cape George was not read by position, so the record's range and focal height (121.3 m) are not used; the story gives the NSLPS 404 ft height above water instead. (10) No wreck or rescue was tied to the station in the sources read. (11) Chronicling America and other newspaper sources were not searched for this station; Canadian newspapers are not in that archive. (12) The Lighthouse Friends visitor note reads 'Grounds open,' and the tower status is not stated. Fact-check 2026-10-27 (independent checker): the 1912 keepers' table row 'Cape George | Alex. McEachern' is on the page image (printed p. 235, scan 242); the appointed-date column is hard to read on that page and is not used. The NSLPS and Lighthouse Friends disagreements on first-light form, 1908 tower height, automation date and ownership are now stated in the text. The 1906-07 'Cape George' lantern entry is ambiguous between the Northumberland Strait and Bras d'Or stations; the story flags it.
